newsitem.title: USA: Three dead, 200,000 without power in New England.
newsitem.headline: Three dead, 200,000 without power in New England.

text.p: Thousands of people were still without electricity in New England Monday three days after the start of a series of vicious storms that dumped up to two feet of snow and torrents of rain in the region.
Three deaths were blamed on the storms, schools in several towns were closed and some residents had to flee their homes because of the lack of heat.

Repair crews from Canada, Pennsylvania, New York and New Jersey were working to restore power to some 200,000 customers in Massachusetts, New Hampshire, Connecticut and Maine after storms Friday and Saturday left up to 24 inches of heavy, wet snow in parts of New England.

Amtrak was forced to cancel its "Vermonter" passenger train and put passengers on buses after snow buried a 120-foot section of track owned by the New England Central Railroad in Claremont, N.H., the railroad said.

New Hampshire state police reported two storm-related deaths. David Blodgett, 34, of Hinsdale died when his snowmobile plowed into a tree and Michele Amaru, 40, of Winchester, died in a two-car crash.

Connecticut state police said a volunteer firefighter in Somers was killed early Sunday when he stepped on a power line while putting out a fire at a neighbor's house. Craig Arnone, 23, died after the oxygen tank he was wearing came in contact with a downed electrical line carrying 23,000 volts.

The Red Cross in Massachusetts, New Hampshire and Connecticut opened shelters to house those who remain without power. Scores of school districts throughout the region canceled classes Monday as people continued digging out.

Northeast Utilities in Connecticut reported 162,000 of its 1.9 million customers remained without power and Massachusetts Electric, a subsidiary of New England Electric Service Service said some 68,000 of its customers were without electricity.

"The storm has caused major damage to our electric distribution centers around the state," said Ian Wilson of New Hampshire Public Service, a Northeast Utilities subsidiary, who added that at its height Saturday's stormed caused a "historic" number of outages -- more than 100,000 in New Hampshire.
Central Maine Power had about 61,000 customers without electricity at the height of the storm Saturday evening. By Monday afternoon, service had been restored to all but 2,500 customers.
And Boston Edison reported some 2,000 of their customers were still awaiting power restoration. At one point some 20,000 of their customers were without power.
